statement: A substance or pair absent from this matrix was NOT checked and is NOT thereby safe. This is a curated mechanism table from primary literature and regulatory reference works, not a comprehensive interaction database, and it is not a substitute for a clinician or pharmacist.

potencyDefinitions.strong: causes a >=5-fold increase in AUC of a sensitive substrate (FDA classification)
potencyDefinitions.moderate: causes a >=2-fold but <5-fold increase in AUC
potencyDefinitions.weak: causes a >=1.25-fold but <2-fold increase in AUC
potencyDefinitions.variable: reported effect differs substantially between studies or preparations
potencyDefinitions.unclear: direction known, magnitude not established in humans

substrates.name: Simvastatin
substrates.note: Sensitive index substrate; grapefruit juice raised AUC roughly sixteen-fold. Accumulation causes myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

substrates.name: Lovastatin
substrates.note: Same lactone chemistry and vulnerability as simvastatin.

substrates.name: Atorvastatin
substrates.note: CYP3A4 substrate with a lower fractional contribution than simvastatin, so a smaller interaction.

substrates.name: Ciclosporin
substrates.note: Inhibition gives nephrotoxicity; induction gives graft rejection. Also a P-glycoprotein substrate.

substrates.name: Tacrolimus
substrates.note: Very narrow window; CYP3A5 expressor status also changes dose requirement.

substrates.name: Midazolam
substrates.note: The standard CYP3A4 probe substrate; oral bioavailability limited by gut and hepatic CYP3A.

substrates.name: Triazolam
substrates.note: Accumulation presents as prolonged sedation and psychomotor impairment.

substrates.name: Alprazolam
substrates.note: CYP3A4 substrate, unlike the glucuronidated benzodiazepines lorazepam, oxazepam and temazepam.

substrates.name: Felodipine
substrates.note: The drug in which the grapefruit interaction was discovered by accident.

substrates.name: Nifedipine
substrates.note: Dihydropyridine; accumulation gives hypotension and reflex tachycardia.

substrates.name: Amiodarone
substrates.note: Substrate and inhibitor at once, with a half-life measured in weeks.

substrates.name: Quinidine
substrates.note: A CYP3A4 substrate that is also the reference strong CYP2D6 inhibitor.

substrates.name: Ergotamine
substrates.note: Accumulation causes ergotism and peripheral ischaemia; the classic macrolide contraindication.

substrates.name: Ritonavir and other HIV protease inhibitors
substrates.note: Substrates and potent inhibitors; the interaction is used deliberately as a booster.

substrates.name: Apixaban
substrates.note: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein substrate; dual inhibition raises bleeding risk.

substrates.name: Rivaroxaban
substrates.note: CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein substrate.

substrates.name: Kinase inhibitors (imatinib, ibrutinib and others)
substrates.note: Oral, high first pass, narrow tolerability; labels frequently carry explicit CYP3A4 dose adjustments.

substrates.name: Ethinylestradiol and progestin contraceptives
substrates.note: Induction causes breakthrough bleeding and contraceptive failure.

substrates.name: Buspirone
substrates.note: Textbook CYP3A4 victim; grapefruit raises exposure severalfold.

substrates.name: Clobazam
substrates.note: Parent drug via CYP3A4; the active N-desmethyl metabolite is cleared by CYP2C19.

substrates.name: Δ9-THC
substrates.note: Metabolised by CYP3A4 alongside CYP2C9, which is dominant for 11-hydroxylation.

substrates.name: Cannabidiol
substrates.note: CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 are the principal oxidative routes, followed by extensive glucuronidation.

substrates.name: Kavalactones
substrates.note: Kava constituents are handled by CYP enzymes including CYP3A4 — the basis of the potentiation claims in the operator corpus.

inhibitors.note: The historical reference strong inhibitor; azole nitrogen coordinates the haem iron.

inhibitors.note: Mechanism-based inactivation of INTESTINAL CYP3A4 by the furanocoumarins bergamottin and 6',7'-dihydroxybergamottin. One 200-300 mL glass suffices; CYP3A recovery takes roughly 24-72 hours, so separating juice from dose within the day does not avoid it. A furanocoumarin-free juice does not reproduce the effect.

substrates.name: Bilirubin (UGT1A1)
substrates.note: The endogenous marker substrate. Reduced UGT1A1 function is Gilbert syndrome; complete deficiency is Crigler-Najjar syndrome.

substrates.name: SN-38, the active metabolite of irinotecan (UGT1A1)
substrates.note: UGT1A1 star-28 and star-6 reduced-function genotypes slow SN-38 inactivation and predict severe neutropenia and diarrhoea; genotype information is on the label.

substrates.name: Lamotrigine (UGT1A4)
substrates.note: Valproate roughly doubles its exposure; carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital and ethinylestradiol roughly halve it. Rash risk is tied to escalation speed, which makes this a safety interaction.

substrates.name: Morphine (UGT2B7)
substrates.note: Conjugated to morphine-3-glucuronide and morphine-6-glucuronide; M6G is itself an active opioid, so this conjugation is not simply inactivation.

substrates.name: Valproate (UGT2B7)
substrates.note: Substrate and inhibitor within the same pathway.

substrates.name: Mycophenolic acid (UGT1A9)
substrates.note: Transplant exposure turns on this isoform; rifampicin induction lowers it.

substrates.name: Propofol (UGT1A9)
substrates.note: Major UGT1A9 substrate.

substrates.name: Zidovudine (UGT2B7)
substrates.note: Glucuronidation is its principal clearance route.

substrates.name: Lorazepam, oxazepam, temazepam
substrates.note: Directly glucuronidated rather than oxidised, which is why they largely escape CYP interactions and are preferred in liver impairment and polypharmacy.

substrates.name: 11-nor-9-carboxy-THC (THC-COOH)
substrates.note: Glucuronidated principally by UGT1A9, with UGT1A3 and UGT2B7 contributions. THC-COOH-glucuronide is the dominant urinary species and the analyte behind a urine cannabinoid screen; confirmatory chromatography hydrolyses it first, which is why free and total carboxy-THC are different numbers.

substrates.name: 11-hydroxy-THC
substrates.note: The psychoactive phase-1 metabolite formed mainly by CYP2C9; oral dosing generates far more of it than inhalation, which explains most of the difference between an edible and an inhaled dose.

substrates.name: Cannabidiol
substrates.note: Glucuronidated by UGT1A9, UGT2B7 and UGT2B17, and a direct substrate as a phenol as well as after oxidation.

substrates.name: Clozapine, olanzapine (UGT1A4)
substrates.note: N-glucuronidation contributes to their clearance alongside CYP1A2.

substrates.name: Amitriptyline, imipramine, trifluoperazine (UGT1A4)
substrates.note: Quaternary N-glucuronides, an unusual conjugate type specific to UGT1A4.

substrates.name: NSAIDs (UGT2B7)
substrates.note: Acyl glucuronides of carboxylic acids are chemically reactive and are implicated in idiosyncratic toxicity — a conjugate that is not simply inert.

inhibitors.name: Valproate
inhibitors.note: The best-documented UGT drug interaction in clinical use: inhibits UGT1A4 and roughly doubles lamotrigine exposure and half-life, so lamotrigine starting doses and escalation steps are halved.

substrates.name: Paracetamol (acetaminophen)
substrates.note: Sulfation carries a substantial fraction at therapeutic doses and SATURATES FIRST as the dose rises, shifting proportionally more of the dose toward glucuronidation and toward CYP2E1 oxidation to NAPQI.

substrates.name: 4-nitrophenol
substrates.note: The standard SULT1A1 probe substrate.

substrates.name: Minoxidil
substrates.note: Requires SULT1A1 sulfonation to its active form — a prodrug on a phase-2 enzyme, which inverts the direction of any inhibition.

substrates.name: Dopamine and noradrenaline (SULT1A3)
substrates.note: Most circulating dopamine is sulfated, and intestinal SULT1A3 is a first-pass barrier for phenolic amines — which is part of why many orally taken monoamines never reach the circulation.

substrates.name: Salbutamol (SULT1A3)
substrates.note: Phenolic amine sulfated in the gut wall on first pass.

substrates.name: Oestradiol (SULT1E1 at low concentration, SULT1A1 higher)
substrates.note: High-affinity oestrogen sulfotransferase contributes to local oestrogen inactivation.

substrates.name: DHEA and bile acids (SULT2A1)
substrates.note: The adrenal and hepatic hydroxysteroid sulfotransferase.

substrates.name: Thyroid hormones (SULT1B1)
substrates.note: Contributes to thyroid hormone handling.

substrates.name: Dietary polyphenols (flavonoids, catechins, quercetin, resveratrol, curcuminoids)
substrates.note: Both substrates and competitors: a phenol-rich botanical competes for the same limited pathway as anything else phenolic present at that moment.

substrates.name: 1'-hydroxysafrole and the 1'-hydroxy metabolites of myristicin and elemicin
substrates.note: BIOACTIVATION, not detoxification: sulfonation gives a 1-prime-sulfooxy ester that ionises to a DNA-binding electrophile. Impaired sulfation (brachymorphic mice, sulfotransferase inhibition) markedly reduces the carcinogenicity, which is the evidence that this conjugate is the hazard. Described as metabolic fate only — no preparation, dosing or combination guidance is given or implied.

inhibitors.name: Curcuminoids (turmeric)
inhibitors.note: Inhibits sulfotransferase activity alongside UGT and multiple CYPs. Clinical consequence depends entirely on achieved systemic curcuminoid concentration, which differs by orders of magnitude between culinary turmeric and a bioavailability-enhanced formulation — and the enhanced formulations are the ones most likely to interact.

substrates.name: Digoxin
substrates.note: The clinical index substrate: a good P-glycoprotein substrate, negligibly CYP metabolised so a change is attributable to transport, and narrow enough in margin to be clinically visible. Also more toxic at an unchanged level when serum potassium falls.

substrates.name: Loperamide
substrates.note: The BLOOD-BRAIN-BARRIER case: a potent opioid agonist that is peripherally restricted only because P-glycoprotein excludes it from the brain. Pump inhibition has been shown to unmask central opioid effects.

substrates.name: Dabigatran etexilate
substrates.note: A pure P-glycoprotein interaction with no CYP component, so it isolates the mechanism — and there is no routine monitoring assay to warn anyone.

substrates.name: Apixaban
substrates.note: P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 substrate; dual inhibition raises bleeding risk substantially.

substrates.name: Rivaroxaban
substrates.note: P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 substrate.

substrates.name: Edoxaban
substrates.note: P-glycoprotein substrate with label-specified dose reduction for inhibitors.

substrates.name: Ciclosporin
substrates.note: Substrate of P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 at once — the archetype of the overlap. Also an inhibitor of both.

substrates.name: Tacrolimus
substrates.note: Dual P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 substrate with a very narrow window.

substrates.name: Fexofenadine
substrates.note: Probe substrate — but also an OATP substrate, which is why fruit juices LOWER rather than raise its exposure. A useful warning that transporters can point in opposite directions.

substrates.name: Colchicine
substrates.note: Dual CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition has caused fatal colchicine toxicity from simultaneous loss of both clearance routes.

substrates.name: HIV protease inhibitors
substrates.note: Substrates as well as inhibitors; brain penetration is relevant to central viral reservoirs.

substrates.name: Kinase inhibitors, anthracyclines, vinca alkaloids, taxanes
substrates.note: P-glycoprotein overexpression in tumour cells is the original multidrug-resistance phenotype the protein was named for.

substrates.name: Quinidine
substrates.note: Substrate AND inhibitor — the same molecule on both sides of the table.

substrates.name: Verapamil
substrates.note: Substrate and the classical inhibitor.

substrates.name: Amiodarone
substrates.note: Substrate and inhibitor with a half-life in weeks.
